key_insight: This paper gives the first full fixed-domain asymptotic theory for joint maximum likelihood estimation of RBF-kernel Gaussian process parameters—variance, lengthscale, and nugget—showing they are consistent, asymptotically normal, and minimax optimal.
engineering_relevance: It provides theoretical support for using standard GP MLE fitting in high-density spatial and scientific applications, with clear guidance on how fast each kernel parameter can be learned.
method: Analyzed joint MLE behavior under fixed-domain asymptotics for the RBF kernel.
Derived consistency, convergence rates, and joint asymptotic normality for spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance.
Proved the rates are minimax optimal.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE, including consistency, rates, and asymptotic normality, but does not mention experiments or datasets.
watch_item: The results are asymptotic and specific to fixed-domain sampling with an RBF kernel, so practical finite-sample behavior and extension to other kernels or sampling regimes may differ.
paper_title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
